RAIN
FALL
OUT OF
CLEAR
SKY

div.head: THE PASSIONATE POET TO HIS LOVE
div.l: stirring our land of wheat and honey
Let us sit on lower ground
to forge our own bespoke chains
made upon the anvil of circumstance
with the soft hammer of your willing smile.

lg.l: The sun is so bright
it blots out the shadows of the cave;
and that is how she brings
eyesight to the blind.
Are we
in love? you
and I, hardly daring to speak
to each other: are we
members of that class after all?
so simply conforming?
extraordinary!
When I gave you toy—birds,
tomorrow—birds, I did not know
they would sing so sweet
a yesterday—song, and for so long.
Bosauquet's blackthorn grows green leaves:
can this tender creeper change so much?
she laughed and said
'It will if you let it'

div.head: LOVE STORY
div.l: It is not for me alone to talk of such things
but this I will say, that when
the lamp looks away, hides in the curtain, when
friends, with fond shy smiles, leave
the recordplayer has to turn itself off,
at such times I think to be in love
and a part of such things
as bring us here, to lie, side
we tell each other tales, and
wait for morning's lies and company

div.head: THE POWER GAME
div.l: web of snares they have laid
lives in fear of strange animals,
And, fawning in her lap, is seized
struggles, strikes once, and then, and then,

lg.l: When you have drunk mugs of tea,
eaten,(two spoons in a bowl)
divide into teams and start the game.
Be gentle: peel off each modest layer
till, naked and blushing, its secret skin
is revealed, crumpled, surprised.
Now you must make it anonymous.
Ignore the sweet smell of disorder
dressing it again, blank and smooth;
be firm: replace each faceless layer.
Lastly, you may disguise yourselves
with eyeshadow, a clean shirt;
take your bag of toys - books,papers,gossip —
and lock the door behind you.
Shadows grow quietly between us
dark pools from an unseen source:
words, like ill—fitting clothes, clinging tighter
sodden, as the waters lap our knees
silently, I on my island, she
perhaps leaving the din of an upperdeck party
to lean on the rail, suddenly alone,
idly watching the stars: and I
poor castaway, with tattered flag and trouser,
wave farewell as the lights drift by.
Or perhaps it is she now come to say farewell
to place a look upon my grave, turning away
to hide in a handkerchief, drowning
my memory in graceful tears.
But no tears fall, as shadowy pools
rise silently between us, as I am bound
in dank cloth of words, as Andromeda unchained
walks over the Stygian waters.

q.l: let me be my own fool of my own making

lg.l: One says to the drunkard, enough
stop drinking (and this
is only fair): to the pagan too
another says, enough, stop
worshipping; that, they say, is false,
this, true.
And this to men who have held
their world in a bottle
or thrown it through the window
the better to see some stars.
Daylight floods all in clarity
adequate and simple explanation.
At night, I hear Sibelius
as pictures flicker through my mind:
mountains and forests, myself alone.
Other people's stories, like mine:
I twist their words too.
Your voice, like treacle toffee
stuck in my teeth, rotting the bone,
every touch of my tongue, agony.
Rotting Bosauauquet in a daze
trying hard to see what hit him,
bangs his head on the same old wall;
so, let the wall go on banging.
It will if you let it.

div.head: DO NOT DESPAIR - ONE OF THE THIEVES WAS SAVED
DO NOT PRESUME — ONE OF THE THIEVES WAS DAMNED
div.l: A man came to the door today
yet shifting, bashful; I did not
let him in, knowing he was a thief:
tonight I found poems by your lover,
staccato pictures, like an oldtime movie,
of two paintings: pears, a boat.
I feared, and now I wonder, whether
he writes poems about you, stealing
like me, a story from your eyes

lg.l: Anything you do
often enough, becomes
in your eyes, important.
So, hidden, I watch walls
we have touched, and
make pictures of how it is
(it being fixed now), establishing thus
a belief, which
she (alas) cannot touch.
